items.text: Among adults aged 65 and over starting a 24-week community strength and balance programme, does an adherence support package added to usual classes, compared with usual classes alone, increase the proportion attending at least two thirds of the 48 sessions?
items.population: Adults aged 65 and over starting the programme in 14 centres in 2027
items.intervention: Weekly reminders, two peer volunteer calls and a home exercise calendar reviewed by the instructor
items.outcome: Attendance at 32 or more of 48 sessions from class registers

finer: Feasible within the programme budget and existing registers; interesting to the region; novel for this package; ethical with consent and equal access to classes; relevant because attendance decides whether the programme works.
summary: One PICOT question with a register-based primary outcome.
